**Finding: COMPLIANT (preferred position).**

The agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on our side:

- **Searches run:** "compete", "competing", "competitor", "exclusive", "field of use", "engage", "solicit", "restriction", "prohibited", "any business other than", "will not engage in" — across all Articles and schedules.
- **Only responsive hits** were (i) boilerplate "court of competent jurisdiction" (p0335, p0469); (ii) no-conflict reps referencing "any contractual restriction binding on or affecting it" (p0240, p0266, p0279) — representations, not covenants; and (iii) the Cap Collateral Account "exclusive control" mechanic (p0387–p0388), which is account-control language, not exclusivity.
- **Servicing is not exclusive:** Section 3.1 simply engages Cellco, and Article VII expressly contemplates our appointing a Successor Servicer.
- **Restrictions we do carry** (Section 9.2 no transfer/Lien, Section 9.5 no petition, Section 9.6 limited recourse) are structural bankruptcy-remoteness covenants, not restrictive covenants on our business activities. Section 7.3's carve-out limiting Cellco's duty to license its servicing software binds the Servicer, not us, so it is not flagged.

No redline proposed.
